correctness.rationale: Independence gives an edge sum; its negative Hessian is a sum of positive-semidefinite rank-one terms with a positive-definite pendant contribution. Thus KKT and continuity of the unique optimum apply. The two-tip stationary split has interior derivatives u/(u+v), v/(u+v). For the boundary argument, a downward crossing of any intermediate positive level r after budget B1 would have the crossing at a budget strictly above r (choose r<x_i*(B1)≤B1), hence at an interior point with positive derivative, impossible. One tip is trivial. A stemless three-tip tree is a star or a pair-clade plus singleton, up to suppression of subdivisions. Strict concavity passes to the pair value function. For a separable budget split, if one group budget fell and another rose, transferring the same small amount from the former to the latter at the first optimum and reversing the transfer at the second would contradict the strict decrease of the corresponding concave secant slopes. This also handles boundaries and the star. Independent exact reconstruction verified the witness gradient, Hessian and normalized inverse sensitivity (-2,18,18,21)/55, with budget about 2.898291333. At an interior point the bordered KKT system is nonsingular; the binary cherry resolution preserves ultrametricity, positivity and the strict negative derivative for small positive resolution length.
residual_risks: The result is local in budget in the four-tip witness and assumes independent extinction, exponential spending response, and no stem. No claim for trees with a stem or correlated extinction.

value.rationale: Management spending is frequently compared across budgets. A sharp minimal topology separates guaranteed nesting from its failure even without ties, zero untreated survival, or unequal root-to-tip distances. The result makes clear why individual optimal allocations need not grow when the total budget grows, despite strict concavity and positive marginal returns. It is a model benchmark, not advice to cut funding.
residual_risks: No empirical fit or generalization to other expenditure-response models is asserted.
